original_question: Find a polynomial-time algorithm that constructs a covering set for a visibility graph matching the optimal asymptotic bit bound.
target_in_paper: Open Problem 43 in §4.9 ("Representing Visibility Graphs"), read together with the immediately preceding paragraph that defines the relevant covering-set representation and with Open Problem 42, which is the "above bound" that Open Problem 43 refers to. Because these statements occur in §4 ("Visibility graph theory: Polygons"), the intended graph class is visibility graphs of simple polygons, not point-visibility or segment-visibility graphs. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the core content of the paper's target problem: it asks for a polynomial-time procedure, the output is a covering set, the object being represented is a visibility graph, and the output should match the asymptotically optimal bit complexity. That is very close to the paper's official wording in Open Problem 43. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
missing_details: The paper's scope here is polygon visibility graphs: in §4, a visibility graph means the visibility graph of a simple polygon. The draft says only "a visibility graph," which is too broad in this survey because the paper separately studies point, segment, and polygon visibility graphs. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

The paper's "covering set" is not arbitrary: it is a family of subgraphs of G such that each member is either a clique or a complete bipartite graph, every member is a subgraph of G, and every edge of G is contained in at least one member of the family. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

The phrase "matching the optimal asymptotic bit bound" should be tied explicitly to Open Problem 42. In the paper, that bound is not yet known; Open Problem 43 asks for a polynomial-time construction that matches the tight asymptotic bit bound sought in Open Problem 42. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

The input/output quantifiers are implicit in the draft. A stand-alone formulation should say: given the visibility graph G of a simple polygon, output such a covering set for G in polynomial time. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))

To stay paper-faithful, the question should remain about compact representation by covering sets, not drift into the separate coordinate-realization question of Open Problem 41. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
refined_question: Given the visibility graph G of a simple polygon with n vertices, construct in polynomial time a covering set F={H1,...,Ht} such that each Hi is either a clique or a complete bipartite subgraph of G, every edge of G belongs to at least one Hi, and the total number of bits needed to encode F matches, up to order notation, the tight asymptotic bound for optimal covering-set representations of n-vertex visibility graphs of simple polygons sought in Open Problem 42. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
justification: The draft matches §4.9 almost uniquely: this is the only place in the survey where "covering set," "bits," and a polynomial-time construction problem appear together. The nearest official formulation is Open Problem 43, and its meaning depends on the immediately preceding paragraph defining the cover model and on Open Problem 42, which asks for the tight asymptotic bit bound that the construction should achieve. The main correction needed is to make explicit that the relevant graphs are visibility graphs of simple polygons, because §4 is the polygon section of the survey. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1012.5187))
